summary:
Astrocare is a mobile-first, offline-first web application that turns astronaut health monitoring into an intuitive, visual daily routine. Instead of forcing crew members to interpret complex medical spreadsheets, Astrocare links real-time vital signs, clinical NEWS2 early-warning scores, psychomotor vigilance testing (PVT), and quick daily habit logs (hydration, nutrition, and exercise) to a responsive 3D biometric avatar. Grounded in real NASA OSDR spaceflight biology datasets and DONKI space weather data, the avatar dynamically reflects fatigue or physiological stress, alerting astronauts before minor issues escalate.

Astrocare directly addresses the challenge by enabling non-physician astronauts to self-assess their health, verify teammates through peer-to-peer Check Crew inspections, and run environment-aware GO / NO-GO readiness evaluations (Earth, Space, or Moon) prior to critical operations like spacewalks. As human missions push toward the Moon and Mars—where communication delays and internet blackouts make real-time Earth support impossible—Astrocare’s autonomous, local-sync architecture safeguards crew survival in deep space while offering a practical blueprint for remote healthcare on Earth.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Astrocare is a mobile-first, offline-first web application designed for continuous astronaut health monitoring, physiological logging, and crew-wide medical collaboration during space missions. Rather than forcing non-physician crew members to interpret complex medical spreadsheets, Astrocare translates biomedical telemetry and daily human-factors logs into an interactive, real-time 3D biometric avatar (circulatory.glb).

The workflow operates through four integrated pillars:

  • Clinical Early-Warning & Biometric Avatar: The 3D avatar reacts dynamically in posture, animation, and color-coded visual cues to the NEWS2 (National Early Warning Score 2) clinical calculation—tracking respiratory rate, oxygen saturation ($\text{SpO}_2$), systolic blood pressure, heart rate, body temperature, and level of consciousness (ACVPU scale)—alongside a Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT) to detect cognitive fatigue.
  • One-Tap Daily Habit Logging: Five quick-action buttons along the bottom of the 3D canvas allow astronauts to log nutrition, hydration, physical exercise (vital for countering bone density and muscle loss), and gastrointestinal/urinary regularity in seconds, triggering immediate feedback on the avatar.
  • Peer-to-Peer Crew Verification (Check Crew): Operating on a flat peer structure, crewmates can inspect each other's avatars and NEWS2 statuses, log objective consciousness assessments, and leave supportive feedback.
  • Environment-Aware GO / NO-GO Readiness Test: Before high-risk activities such as spacewalks (EVAs) or docking maneuvers, astronauts run a readiness evaluation contextualized to their current mission environment (Earth, Space, or Moon), receiving an immediate GO or NO-GO clearance signal.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Cognitive Offloading & Early Detection: Replaces exhausting raw data tables with glanceable visual diagnostics, enabling early intervention before minor physiological deviations escalate into medical emergencies.
  • Deep-Space Autonomy: Engineered for Artemis lunar bases and Mars transit missions where communication latency (up to 20+ minutes each way) and signal blackouts prevent real-time Flight Surgeon supervision.
  • Dual-Use Terrestrial Impact: Its lightweight browser architecture and offline synchronization provide a scalable blueprint for rural clinics, disaster-response teams, polar expeditions, and remote communities on Earth with limited connectivity and medical staff.

Tools, Languages, Software & Data Used

  • Architecture & Languages: Full-stack TypeScript monorepo unifying shared clinical schemas, NEWS2 scoring logic, and validation models across client and server.
  • Frontend & 3D Visualization: React, Vite, HTML5/CSS3, and WebGL/3D rendering (Avatar3D.tsx, circulatory.glb) with a responsive mobile-first UI (BodyPanel, MonitorPanel, PvtPanel, CrewStrip).
  • Backend & Data Pipelines: Node.js / TypeScript server (index.ts, telemetry.ts, store.ts, data.ts) with automated ingestion scripts (fetch-data.ts) that parse and normalize real spaceflight datasets from NASA OSDR (SpaceX Inspiration4 hematology OSD-569 / LSDS-7 and metabolic panels OSD-575 / LSDS-8) and NASA DONKI (Geomagnetic Storm GST and Solar Energetic Particle SEP radiation records).

Creativity & Innovation

Astrocare reimagines clinical aerospace telemetry through the approachable mental model of a virtual companion (inspired by Nintendogs, Pokémon GO, and Pou), where the "companion" is a 3D representation of the astronaut's own body. By pairing gamified daily care habits with hospital-grade NEWS2 clinical rigor, cognitive PVT reaction testing, and peer-to-peer crew accountability, Astrocare turns mandatory medical compliance into an engaging, intuitive daily ritual.

Key Factors Considered

  • Connectivity & Resilience (Offline-First Dual Sync): Built to operate with 100% functionality offline using local browser persistence, synchronizing peer-to-peer over a spacecraft or habitat Local Area Network (LAN), and automatically reconciling telemetry with NASA's OSDR when Earth uplink windows open.
  • Accessibility & Human Factors: Designed specifically for non-medical crew members operating under high stress and microgravity—featuring large touch targets, color-coded NEWS2 legends, plain-language guidance, and immediate visual indicators.
  • Cost & Energy Efficiency: Runs directly in any standard smartphone or tablet web browser without requiring proprietary medical hardware, heavy native installations, or continuous high-bandwidth satellite uplinks, minimizing both mission payload mass and device power consumption.
